hints.title: Definition of Happy String
hints.text: A string is happy if it contains only a, b, and c, and no two consecutive characters are identical.

hints.title: Total Count of Happy Strings
hints.text: For length n, there are 3 * 2^(n - 1) possible happy strings. If k exceeds this total, return an empty string.

hints.title: Lexicographical Generation
hints.text: Generate strings using depth-first search trying a, b, c in alphabetical order, or calculate character-by-character mathematically.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def getHappyString(self, n: int, k: int) -> str:
        total = 3 * (1 << (n - 1))
        if k > total:
            return ""
        k -= 1
        first_char_idx = k // (1 << (n - 1))
        res = [["a", "b", "c"][first_char_idx]]
        k %= (1 << (n - 1))
        for i in range(1, n):
            options = [c for c in ["a", "b", "c"] if c != res[-1]]
            branch_size = 1 << (n - 1 - i)
            choice = k // branch_size
            res.append(options[choice])
            k %= branch_size
        return "".join(res)
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 3^N strings then filtering non-happy ones does unnecessary work.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Calculating the k-th sequence mathematically based on branch sizes (powers of 2) runs in O(N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate realizes branch choices have size 2^(remaining) and selects the prefix without full search.
